It says `MarkDone` must conditionally accept the current token, but does not explicitly require the comparison and rejection to be atomic.
It states that “lease fencing alone cannot protect the remote effect” and requires remote-enforced durable operation identity or authoritative-status reconciliation before retry.

It calls renewal errors ambiguous and requires stopping admission before the last definitely effective lease expires, but does not require authoritative confirmation or stopping all further effects immediately upon uncertainty.
The renewal goroutine is never discussed in terms of cancellation, joining, ownership by `Run`, or shutdown before `Release`/return.
It requires release to compare acquisition identity and fencing token atomically so only the exact current lease can be deleted.
It explicitly schedules an `Apply` effect whose response is lost, followed by a retry whose effect also occurs.
It requires every retry and successor to reuse a durable operation identity enforced remotely, or reconcile authoritative status before retrying.
It explicitly notes that all three `Apply` attempts can fail before taking effect while `MarkDone` still permanently declares completion.
It states that the `MarkDone` error is ignored and requires completion-write failure not to be treated as successful processing.
It never quantifies the cross-owner maximum as six remote-effect attempts.
It does not require one end-to-end deadline or classify transient, permanent, and ambiguous failures before retry.
It explicitly rejects the idea that lease renewal alone is sufficient: “lease fencing alone cannot protect the remote effect.”
It identifies continued work after uncertain renewal as a bug and requires stopping admission; it does not endorse unrestricted continuation.
It requires reuse of one stable durable operation identity, not retry under a fresh identity.
It criticizes ignored Renew and MarkDone errors and requires conditional Release; it does not approve discarding those errors.
verdict.summary: The candidate identifies the main duplicate-effect, stale-owner, false-completion, completion-write, and stale-release failures. It misses the renewal-goroutine lifecycle, six-attempt bound, end-to-end retry policy, and fully explicit atomic/stop-after-uncertainty requirements.
